title: How to Choose Your First Target Area
subtitle: Not the biggest room, and not the one you feel worst about. The smallest space that will still feel like a real win.
hands_off_to: Part Two, Prepare (Chapter 5, The 6S Home Audit)
audience: Readers who now understand the 6S method and feel motivated to start, but risk starting too big. Busy home keepers and parents prone to overwhelm and burnout. New to applying the method.
core_promise: Choose one first target you can actually win, using a one-minute decision tool, and leave the chapter with that target named and written down.
emotional_purpose: Relief from overwhelm and protection of momentum. Replace the urge to attack the hardest room with the confidence of a small, smart, winnable choice.
practical_purpose: Teach the friction-versus-effort decision (the First Target Map), steer the reader away from the garage trap, give three filters for the best target, and end with a scored shortlist and one committed target.
primary_cta: Choose your first target: list three to five annoying spaces, score friction and effort, subtract effort from friction, pick the winner, and write it down. Read the chapter free in the online book.
secondary_cta: Read the chapter free online, then continue to Chapter 5 to see your target clearly before you touch it.
keywords: how to choose what to organize first
should I start with the garage
how to stay motivated to declutter
hero_device: The First Target Map (friction vs effort two-by-two; sweet spot is high friction, low effort)
three_filters: win where you will see it (daily-touch)
definition: The best first target is the smallest space that will still feel like a real win. High friction, low effort. Big daily relief, small one-time cost.
one_idea_to_keep: You do not need more motivation to start. You need a smaller, smarter first target. Win where you will see it, and the next project gets easier on its own.
